page.title: Sessions
page.purpose: Show what a live kernel is holding: the variables bound so far, the grants it runs under, how close it is to its ceilings, and why a reclaimed session ended.

priorities.statement: The variable inspector obeys the same handle discipline it displays.
priorities.notes: Variables render as bounded representations. Materializing one in the console is an explicit, recorded operator action — never an incidental read. A console that eagerly renders payloads contradicts the product inside its own interface and becomes a way around the boundary.

priorities.statement: Grants held are legible before anything is submitted.
priorities.notes: A reader should be able to answer 'could this session call something destructive' without running anything.

priorities.statement: A reclaimed session states why it was reclaimed.
priorities.notes: Idle, wall-clock, or memory. A session that simply disappears is indistinguishable from a crash.

priorities.statement: Proximity to a ceiling is visible before the ceiling is hit.
priorities.notes: Reclamation should be predictable from the page, not a surprise reported after the fact.

priorities.statement: Sandbox binding is stated when present.
priorities.notes: Whether a session's filesystem effects are isolated changes how much a reader should trust what it did.

states.description: Live sessions are listed; a selected session shows its variables, grants, and ceilings.
No session is live. The page explains that sessions are created by agents and are per-run, not long-lived.
The selected session is executing a program; variables and ceilings update as it proceeds.
The selected session has ended and states which ceiling or idle rule reclaimed it.
A variable's contents were requested but the operator's grant does not permit materialization.
Session state could not be read and the reason is visible.

elements.name: Live sessions
elements.description: One row per session: id, owner, age, grants, program count, ceiling proximity.

elements.name: Kernel variables
elements.description: Name, type, and bounded representation for each bound variable. Contents are not rendered by default.

elements.name: Materialize variable
elements.description: Explicitly renders a variable's contents and records the operator action.

elements.name: Ceiling usage
elements.description: Wall-clock, memory, and idle time against their configured limits.

elements.name: Workspace sandbox
elements.description: Whether the session is bound to an isolated workspace.

elements.name: Execution output
elements.description: Invocations and output as they complete, for the session's running program.

claims.statement: The page exposes a named sessions region containing the session list.
Kernel variables render as bounded representations; contents appear only after an explicit materialize action.
claims.rationale: OT-P0-003. The console must not become a path that reads full payloads without crossing the same boundary a program crosses.

claims.statement: Materializing a variable from the console is recorded as an operator action rather than treated as a free read.
claims.rationale: An unrecorded console read is an ungoverned egress path with no provenance, which is precisely what the binding boundary exists to prevent.

claims.statement: The grants a session holds are shown without needing to run anything.
A reclaimed session names the rule that reclaimed it — idle, wall-clock, or memory.
claims.rationale: OT-P1-005. A session that ends without a stated reason is indistinguishable from a crash, and an agent that lost state deserves a better answer than silence.

claims.statement: Proximity to a ceiling is conveyed by value and text as well as by any color treatment.
claims.rationale: The accessibility floor forbids status carried by color alone, and this is the status that predicts losing kernel state.

claims.statement: A materialization the operator's grant does not permit is refused with a stated reason rather than rendering empty.
claims.rationale: An empty render is indistinguishable from an empty variable.

claims.statement: Loading, empty, running, reclaimed, permission-denied, and error states each render dedicated content.
The session list, the variable inspector, and the materialize action are reachable by keyboard alone.
